summary.intent: Aggregate and act on parallel standards/spec review findings for PR #618 (core det-cbor KAT spine) while tracking other in-flight background agents (#624 API auth slice, #623 engine scaffold, #645 Tauri shell).
summary.outcome: Fixed all actionable findings from the #618 standards review — extended the CI rust path filter to include .cargo/config.toml, fixed kat_gen.rs so manifest regeneration no longer silently preserves stale fields from the existing file, and documented the trust/malformed classification rationale in error.rs — then regenerated vectors (byte-identical), reran tests/clippy/fmt/actionlint/wasm leg all green, and committed. Separately verified #624's completion report against disk (branch, 2 commits, clean tree) before trusting it.

repo: CI's `rust` path filter (.github/workflows/ci.yml) must include .cargo/config.toml — a wasmtime runner config change was silently skipping the core-kats job otherwise

kat_gen.rs's build_manifest was preserving manifestVersion/profile/structureTags/kdfEdges from the existing file on regeneration, letting hand-edits survive and weakening the 'committed generator is the only writer' invariant — now fixed to always regenerate from source

crates/core/src/error.rs trust/malformed boundary (indefinite-length CBOR = trust-layer failure; tags/floats/oversize simple values = malformed) is a judgment call not derivable from blueprint/core.md and needed explicit documentation rather than folklore
Commit subject format convention in this repo: no parentheses in the subject line
Manifest schema structs are duplicated between tests/kat_manifest.rs (Deserialize) and examples/kat_gen.rs (Serialize) — a baseline smell left unfixed as a judgment call
Check names in error.rs are spelled twice per variant (CHECKS const + check() match arm) — a uniqueness test backstops drift but a table-driven macro would collapse the duplication

code.finding: rust path filter was missing .cargo/config.toml, letting wasmtime runner config changes skip core-kats
build_manifest preserved manifestVersion/profile/structureTags/kdfEdges from the pre-existing file instead of the freshly generated source, allowing hand-edits to survive regen undetected
trust vs malformed classification boundary documented inline as an explicit, deliberate design decision rather than an implicit one

workflow: Standard pattern here: after a commit, dispatch parallel Standards-review and Spec-review agents on the diff, aggregate both reports, fix real findings, then open the PR and register the required CI check
Never take a background agent's self-report at face value — verify branch/commits/clean-tree on disk before summarizing its work to the user
Multiple independent background agents (review agents, implementation agents for other PRs) run concurrently and their task-notifications interleave; need to track each thread's state independently

friction: Task notifications for unrelated background work (#624 finishing) arrived while still waiting on #618's review agents, requiring context-juggling between two PR threads
The KAT generator's silent field-preservation bug (kat_gen.rs) meant the 'committed generator is sole writer' guarantee was not actually enforced — only caught via review, not via existing tests
open_items: #618 PR not yet opened and its required CI check not yet registered in branch protection, despite fixes being committed

Confirm 'Core KATs (native + WASM)' is actually configured as a merge-blocking required check, not just a named CI job (flagged by the standards review, not yet confirmed)
